# Context

You have been hired to determine the risk of quagga mussel establishment into water bodies of the western US (e.g. Lake Tahoe). Use the questions below to analyze survival rates and the survival curve of mussels under different calcium concentrations. Calcium is critical for mussel growth and physiology

# Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
```

# Load data

```{r}
raw_quagga <- read.csv(here("data", "Davis_quagga_mussels.csv"))
```

# Question 1

### Q1 Part 1

Convert data into tibble

```{r}
quagga_tibble <- as_tibble(raw_quagga) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("9_ppm_Ca", "12_ppm_Ca")))

print(quagga_tibble)
```

### Q1 Part 2

Using the provided data, create a survival object and fit the survival curves separately by treatment

```{r}
quagga_sfit <- survfit(Surv(day, status) ~ treatment, data = quagga_tibble)

plot(quagga_sfit)
```

### Q1 Part 3

Show/Provide the life tables for both treatments (a life table presents information on the number at risk (number still remaining) and the cumulative survival at that instant).

```{r}
summary(quagga_sfit)$table

summary(quagga_sfit)
```

# Question 2

### Q2 Part 1

Now that a survival curve fits the data, visualize it with a Kaplan-Meier plot using the survminer package and the ggsurvplot() function. Show your plot.

```{r}
ggsurvplot(quagga_sfit)
```

### Q2 Part 2

Compare the survival outcomes of the 2 treatments. Which treatment appears more effective? Why? And what do the “+” symbols on the curves represent?

-   A calcium concentration of 12ppm appears to be more effective because 100% probability of survival persists for a greater amount of time and survival remains higher in this concentration up until the final time point. The “+” symbols represent censored data points.

# Question 3

### Q3 Part 1

Now add confidence intervals to your plot, show the p-value for the log-rank test visually, show a risk table below the plot, and change the colors and the group labels.

```{r}
ggsurvplot(quagga_sfit, conf.int = TRUE, pval = TRUE, 
           risk.table = TRUE, 
           legend.labs = c("9 ppm", "12 ppm"), legend.title = "Treatment",  
           palette = c("purple", "darkgreen"), 
           title = "Kaplan-Meier Curve for Quagga Mussel Survival", 
           risk.table.height = 0.35)
```

### Q3 Part 2

Interpret the p-value from the log-rank test. What does this p-value indicate about the difference in survival probabilities between the two calcium treatments?

-   The value p = 0.005 indicates that it is possible to reject the null hypothesis that there is no difference in survival probabilities between the two calcium treatments.
